threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: If you still call it a ‘bus stop’ instead of a ‘bus shelter,’ you’re definitely new around here. Locals just know.
Last night on the 196, a guy tucked into a full fish and chips meal like it was a five-star restaurant. The smell was something else.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last Sunday, I saw a guy walking his ferret on a leash near the canal. That’s when it hit me—only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a carnival-like pop-up bar in an abandoned factory, serving cocktails alongside DJ sets while graffiti artists paint live.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they side-eye BART delays; the rest just complain about late trains without knowing the real chaos of the Transbay Tube.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a guy practicing his stand-up routine; he didn’t miss a beat even with the bumps. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into the plaça and find a taverna; locals know that the best vermut is in the tiny bars down the side streets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their confused face at the Diagonal metro station during rush hour. It’s like navigating a maze!

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Dalston Junction station is the 'main' one, not realizing it’s all about that sneaky London Overground.
Last night on the 133, a guy argued with the driver about the right stops, then offered to pay in Monopoly money. The driver just shook his head, laughing.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a panda onesie calmly ordering a döner at 3 AM, I knew this place was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip a beer while standing in a pop-up gallery, surrounded by street art and the hum of hipster conversations spilling onto the sidewalk.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a true local when they can navigate the BART delays while still gripping a burrito, like it's a rite of passage, not a setback.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 Balboa this morning with a mix of tourists and locals. One guy serenaded us with a ukulele—only in the TL would you get a concert mid-commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the casa modernista are in Eixample, but the quirky ones hiding in Gràcia's backstreets are true gems. Most just stroll past.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their still-fresh, unscuffed shoes; locals know you need sturdier ones for the cobblestone streets.
